CHIEF COMPLAINT
Post-operative evaluation following bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 36-year-old female returning for post-operative evaluation of bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on 10/10/2020. She reports her breasts are healing well. A lump was previously noted under the left breast during a visit in March with PA Ruth Sanchez; however, patient has not felt it since that time and has been performing massages. Patient reports scar widening and has been applying scar gel daily. Previous back pain has resolved. Otherwise, patient is doing well and enjoying summertime.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, and vomiting. Denies current back pain. Denies any new lumps, bumps, or hard spots noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty (10/10/2020).

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Enjoying summertime.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Bilateral breasts: Incisions are well healed with no signs of infection or redness. Scar widening noted, particularly in one area with high tension. No lumps palpated.

RESULTS
Photographs taken today for follow-up documentation.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Patient is status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty with good healing without complications. Scar widening noted in one area with high tension. Doctor notes that previous lump is likely scar tissue. Patient declines scar revision at this time and understands that revision would not be considered until at least one year post-operatively. Plan: Continue Mederma scar gel twice daily with massage therapy. Follow-up appointment in 6 months to reassess scars and discuss potential revision options. Photographs obtained for comparison at follow-up visit.
